title: Vector Clipping (Child Nesting) vs Vector Masking
subtitle: Thumbnail Drop vs Body Drop, Insert Inside & Unmasking

learningObjectives: Master the fundamental architectural difference between Vector Clipping (child nesting) and Vector Masking.
Execute Vector Clipping by dragging an artwork layer onto the text body of a parent container.
Execute Vector Masking by docking a vector path onto the thumbnail icon of a target layer.
Utilize the top toolbar 'Insert inside the selection' toggle (Ctrl+Alt+X / Cmd+Opt+X) for real-time contained drawing.
Release, extract, and re-order nested layers without breaking geometry or causing accidental flattening.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: Many vector artists conflate 'clipping' and 'masking', using the terms interchangeably. In Affinity Designer, they represent two radically different mathematical and scene graph operations: (1) Vector Clipping (Child Nesting): An object becomes a child nested physically inside a parent vector shape. The parent acts as a visible cookie cutter, retaining its own fill and stroke while constraining the child's visibility to its interior; (2) Vector Masking: A vector curve is attached to a layer as a pure alpha/boundary stencil. The mask path itself becomes invisible (losing its own fill and stroke), dictating strictly where the parent layer shows through. Mastering the physical drag drop-zones in the Layers panel is key to commanding this engine.

technicalEvidence.source: Affinity Designer 3.3.3 Vector Clipping & Masking Architecture Specification

toolAndFeatureExplanation.persona: Vector Persona (Layers Studio Drag Zones & Top Toolbar)
toolAndFeatureExplanation.description: Controlled via physical drag drop-zones in the Layers Studio or the 'Insert Inside' toggle on the top toolbar.
contextBarOptions: Insert at top of layer (default drafting behavior)
Insert behind selection (places new objects directly under active selection)
Insert inside the selection (automatically nests new drawings as children inside active shape)
Drop onto Layer Label: Creates a Vector Clipping hierarchy (nested child)
Drop onto Layer Thumbnail: Creates a Vector Mask hierarchy (attached stencil)

stepByStepInstructions.title: Create a Parent Vector Container
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Draw a large circle and give it a vibrant teal fill `#00d2ff`. This will serve as your parent container shape.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Draw Overflowing Content
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Draw a jagged polygon or a series of diagonal stripes that extend far outside the boundaries of the teal circle.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Perform Vector Clipping (Body Drop)
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: In the Layers Studio, click and drag the stripes layer directly over the text name/body of the teal circle layer (notice a horizontal blue indent line appear). Release the mouse. The stripes are instantly clipped inside the circle, while the teal background and circle stroke remain completely intact!

stepByStepInstructions.title: Perform Vector Masking (Thumbnail Drop)
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Create a fresh rectangle filled with a photo or gradient. Draw a star shape above it. In the Layers Studio, drag the star layer and drop it directly onto the square THUMBNAIL icon of the rectangle (notice a vertical drop line appear right beside the thumbnail). The star becomes an attached vector mask!

stepByStepInstructions.title: Use the 'Insert Inside' Toolbar Toggle
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Select any vector shape. On the top toolbar, click the 'Insert inside the selection' button (circle with an arrow pointing into a square). Now select the Paint Brush or Pen Tool and draw freely. Notice everything you draw automatically nests inside the selected shape without needing manual drag-and-drop in the Layers panel!

visualExamples.title: Vector Clipping vs Vector Masking Matrix
visualExamples.description: Crucial mechanical differences between the two methods.
visualExamples.visualContent:
| Feature | Vector Clipping (Child Nesting) | Vector Masking (Thumbnail Dock) |
|---|---|---|
| Drop Target in Layers Panel | Drag onto the Layer Text / Body | Drag onto the Layer Thumbnail Icon |
| Drop Indicator Bar | Horizontal indented line under parent | Vertical line attached to thumbnail |
| Container Fill / Stroke | KEPT (Parent circle retains fill & stroke) | LOST (Mask shape becomes transparent stencil) |
| Child Layer Freedom | Child can be moved freely inside bounds | Parent artwork moves; mask stencil stays fixed |
| Multiple Items Inside | Can hold unlimited nested children | Single vector mask path per layer |

guidedPractice.title: Constructing a Planet with Shadow & Crater Clips
guidedPractice.taskDescription: Construct a cosmic planet sphere with an atmospheric shadow crescent and surface craters nested cleanly using vector clipping.
checkpoints: Draw base planet circle filled with warm orange `#f97316`.
Enable 'Insert inside the selection' on the top toolbar.
Draw a dark shadow crescent shape across the lower-right half. Notice it clips inside the sphere instantly.
Draw several circular craters overlapping the planet edge. Notice they clip cleanly without spilling into space.
Select the craters with the Move Tool and adjust their positions freely inside the planet sphere.
guidedPractice.expectedOutcome: A celestial illustration where multiple interior shading and detail layers are non-destructively clipped inside the parent sphere.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Parent shape loses its color fill when trying to clip
commonPitfalls.cause: Accidentally dropping the shape onto the THUMBNAIL (creating a mask) instead of the BODY (creating a clipping child).
commonPitfalls.solution: Drag the layer out to undo. Drag it carefully onto the text label area of the parent layer until a horizontal indented line appears.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Cannot select or move a clipped child with the Move Tool
commonPitfalls.cause: Auto-select is selecting the parent container instead of the child.
commonPitfalls.solution: Double-click directly on the child artwork on the canvas, or select the child layer directly inside the Layers Studio.

commonPitfalls.cause: Dragging an object onto the artboard header instead of a specific shape layer.
commonPitfalls.solution: Check layer indentation in the Layers panel; keep objects organized under designated shape parents.

knowledgeCheck.question: In the Affinity Designer Layers Studio, how do you create a Vector Clipping hierarchy where a child layer is clipped inside a parent shape?
options: Drag the child layer directly onto the text name / body area of the parent layer (horizontal indented drop bar).
Drag the child layer onto the trash can icon.
Hold Alt+F4 while clicking the canvas.
Convert the document to a PDF.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Dropping a layer onto the text body of another layer indents it as a child clip, constraining its visible boundaries while preserving the parent's fill and stroke.

knowledgeCheck.question: What happens to a vector shape when it is dragged onto the THUMBNAIL icon of a target layer to become a Vector Mask?
options: Its original fill and stroke become invisible, functioning purely as a geometric stencil that dictates where the target layer is revealed.
It changes color to pure black.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: A vector mask sheds its visible cosmetic styling and acts purely as an alpha/boundary stencil docked to the parent thumbnail.

knowledgeCheck.question: Which top toolbar toggle allows you to draw new vector shapes that automatically nest inside the currently selected object as child clips?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The 'Insert inside the selection' toggle automatically channels all newly drawn paths and strokes directly into the active shape as non-destructive child clips.

summaryPoints: Vector Clipping nests objects as children inside a visible parent shape (Body Drop).
Vector Masking docks a vector curve as an invisible stencil onto a layer thumbnail (Thumbnail Drop).
'Insert Inside' automates child clipping directly from the top toolbar.
Clipped child objects can be repositioned and animated freely without altering parent bounds.

slides.title: Vector Clipping (Child Nesting) vs Vector Masking
slides.subtitle: Mastering the Two Fundamental Containment Paradigms
slides.contentMarkdown:
Welcome to **Lesson D05-02**.

One of the most common points of confusion in digital design is the difference between **Clipping** and **Masking**.

In this lesson, you will master Affinity Designer's physical drop-zone mechanics in the Layers Studio, and learn when to use **Child Nesting** (clipping) versus **Thumbnail Docking** (masking).

actionBox.label: Mastery Insight
actionBox.text: Dropping onto the Layer Body creates a Clip. Dropping onto the Thumbnail creates a Mask.

slides.title: The Core Mechanical Difference
slides.subtitle: Parent Container vs Alpha Stencil
slides.contentMarkdown:
Affinity Designer distinguishes clearly between:

1. **Vector Clipping (Child Nesting):**
   - The parent shape **keeps its own fill and stroke**.
   - Child layers sit inside, clipped by the parent's boundary.
   - Ideal for adding textures, stripes, and shadows inside buttons and characters.
2. **Vector Masking (Thumbnail Docking):**
   - The masking shape **loses its fill and stroke**, becoming an invisible stencil.
   - It clips the target layer to its silhouette.
   - Ideal for cropping illustrations or photos into custom geometric shapes.

visual.content: Vector Clipping: Parent Fill is KEPT (Visible Container) VS Vector Masking: Mask Fill is LOST (Invisible Stencil)

slides.title: Layers Studio Drop Zones Demystified
slides.subtitle: The Two Physical Drop Targets in Every Layer Row
slides.contentMarkdown:
Look closely at any layer row in the Layers Studio:

- **Drop Zone 1: The Thumbnail Icon (Left):**
  - Dragging a layer here displays a **vertical drop indicator**.
  - Results in an attached **Vector Mask**.
- **Drop Zone 2: The Text Label / Row Body (Right):**
  - Dragging a layer here displays an **indented horizontal line**.
  - Results in a **Vector Clipping Child**.

visual.content:
Layer Row:  [Thumbnail] ─────────────── [Layer Name / Label Body]
                 ▲                                    ▲
          Drop on Thumbnail                     Drop on Text Body
        = Attached Vector Mask                = Nested Vector Child Clip

slides.title: Step-by-Step: Executing a Vector Clip
slides.subtitle: Nesting Stripes Inside an App Icon
slides.contentMarkdown:
Follow these steps to clip decorative stripes inside an icon base:

1. **Step 1:** Draw a rounded rectangle and fill it with deep royal blue `#1e3a8a`.
2. **Step 2:** Draw 3 diagonal yellow stripes that run completely across the canvas.
3. **Step 3:** Open the Layers Studio (`F7`).
4. **Step 4:** Drag the stripes layer onto the **text name** of the rounded rectangle.
5. **Inspect:** The stripes instantly vanish outside the rounded rectangle edges, but remain 100% visible inside! Select the stripes with the Move Tool (`V`) to reposition them freely.

actionBox.label: Pro Shortcut
actionBox.text: Double-click directly on the stripes on the canvas to select the child without hunting in the Layers panel.

slides.title: The 'Insert Inside' Toolbar Engine
slides.subtitle: Drafting Directly Inside Containers
slides.contentMarkdown:
You don't need to drag layers in the panel every time! The top main toolbar features **Drafting Target Toggles**:

1. **Insert at top of layer:** Standard behavior (new items appear at the top of the stack).
2. **Insert behind selection:** Places newly drawn shapes underneath the selected object.
3. **Insert inside the selection:** Any path, brush stroke, or shape you draw next is **automatically nested as a child clip** inside the active selection!

actionBox.label: Workflow Accelerator
actionBox.text: Select a character body, turn on 'Insert Inside', and paint shadows freely without worrying about spilling outside.

slides.title: Releasing and Unmasking Layers
slides.subtitle: Extracting Children Without Data Loss
slides.contentMarkdown:
If you ever need to extract or reorder a clipped layer:

1. Expand the parent layer in the Layers Studio to reveal its nested children.
2. Click and drag the child upward or downward **past the left margin** until a full-width non-indented horizontal bar appears.
3. Release the mouse. The child is liberated back to the root layer stack, completely unclipped and intact!

visual.content: Expand Parent | Drag to Left Margin | Full-Width Drop Bar = Unclipped

slides.title: Clipping & Masking Traps
slides.subtitle: Diagnose Common UI Confusion
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Shape Lost Its Color (Accidental Mask)
- **The Issue:** You wanted to clip stripes inside a red circle, but the circle turned invisible and only the stripes show.
- **The Cause:** You dropped the circle onto the stripes' thumbnail.
- **The Fix:** Drag the circle out to restore its fill. Drag the stripes onto the *body* of the red circle.

### 2. Can't Move Mask Independently
- **The Issue:** Moving an image moves the mask along with it.
- **The Fix:** On the Context Toolbar, enable **'Lock Children'** so you can reposition the artwork while the mask remains anchored.

visual.content: Body Drop = Retain Fill | Thumbnail Drop = Stencil | Lock Children = Decouple Movement

slides.title: Independent Challenge: Celestial Vector Terrarium
slides.subtitle: Put Clipping & Masking into Practice
slides.contentMarkdown:
### Your Mission:
Construct a botanical terrarium contained inside a glass flask:

1. Draw a glass flask silhouette.
2. Use **Vector Masking** (thumbnail dock) to mask an organic landscape painting inside the glass flask.
3. Select the soil bed layer inside the flask, activate **'Insert inside the selection'**, and draw plant roots that automatically clip to the soil.
4. Add a highlight glare curve nested inside the glass flask rim.

### Acceptance Criteria:
- Landscape masked cleanly to flask shape.
- Plant roots clipped non-destructively to the soil container.
- Move Tool allows adjusting roots without breaking flask bounds.
